key_insight: The paper shows that the usual assumptions used to relate homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization are too weak to close the time-complexity gap, and that only a stronger combined assumption set can recover the best-known homogeneous-style scaling.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this clarifies when asynchronous training can safely rely on faster heterogeneous workers without paying an unavoidable theoretical penalty in wall-clock convergence time.
method: Proves impossibility results under standard first- and second-order similarity assumptions for any randomized algorithm.
Tests the interpolation regime and shows weak interpolation alone still cannot bridge the gap.
Introduces a minimal combination of strong interpolation and the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition to obtain a sharper time-complexity bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity analysis and lower-bound/impossibility proofs rather than empirical experiments or dataset-based evaluation.
watch_item: The improved bound depends on stronger structural assumptions, so it may not apply to real systems with highly nonuniform data or weak local optimization geometry.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
